gate.notes:
All 13 reader verdicts were confirmed from source; none changed. The reader's one imprecise site was the pettype-add miss: it cited pettype-add.component.ts:31, a line inside the subscribe callback, while the emit that settles the case is on line 33. I cited :33.

Systematic graph pattern behind the 5 spurious extras: every navigate of the form router.navigate(['/owners', x]) (owner-edit.ts:70, pet-add.ts:90, visit-add.ts:102, visit-edit.ts:98) is recorded as a 'may' edge to longer owners/:id/* routes (edit, pets/add) as well as to owners/:id. Angular never splits a non-first command on '/', so those targets are unreachable from these calls. The extractor seems to treat a two-segment array with a dynamic tail as a prefix wildcard; it should be an exact-length match.

Reference pattern: the 3 'e' misses come from Rima's GT attributing a transition to the route that a component is registered under (PettypeAddComponent -> pettypes/add, VisitAddComponent -> pets/:id/visits/add) or to '**', not to where the trigger actually navigates.
